blogs.title: Can We Keep What We Learned And Still Adapt? The Power Of Orthogonal Fine‑Tuning
blogs.description: Explore how multiplying a frozen model by an orthogonal matrix preserves the geometry of learned representations—keeping pairwise angles and spectral norms intact—so models can adapt without losing what they already know.

blogs.title: The Sized Problem in Orthogonal Fine‑Tuning
blogs.description: Delve into why ordinary OFT uses huge Ø(dØ²) parameter budgets, how block‑diagonal shortcuts cut costs at the price of expressiveness, and why those trade‑offs limit practical adoption.

blogs.title: "Fast Fourier Tricks” Made Tiny – How Butterfly Structures Cut Parameters
blogs.description: Discover the Cooley‑Tukey butterfly graph from radio astronomy turned into a compact recipe for building dense orthogonal matrices with only O(d log d) trainable numbers—an elegant blend of computation and storage savings.

blogs.title: "Orthogonal Butterfly" (BOFT): Bringing Speed, Size & Generality Together
blogs.description: Unpack the full BOFT pipeline—Cayley‑parameterized factorized butterflies, identity warmup, multiplicative dropout—and see how it turns any foundation model into a fine‑tuned champion across vision, language and diffusion tasks.

blogs.title: "More Than Pointers": Why BOFT’s Structured Matrix Gives Models Better Generalization
blogs.description: Learn how BOFT’s restricted subclass of orthogonal matrices behaves like known fast transforms (FFT, Hadamard), preserves spectral norms naturally, and imposes an inductive bias that keeps learning stable while avoiding overfitting.

blogs.title: "Not All Gains Are Equal": Where BOFT Still Stumbles & Future Directions
blogs.description: Address the lingering runtime overhead from repeated sparse multiplications, discuss open questions about optimal network topologies for information transmission, and outline where researchers might push BOFT even further.
